summary: Franz Xaver Erhard is a scholar in Tibetology. He completed master's studies at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann (1793–1862) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Rostock (~1812–1817) and held a post at Kazan Imperial University from around 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard (born 1953) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1998) under Lambert Schmithausen, served at the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993), and was a professor at the University of Munich (2003–2019).
François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Lyon from 1950 to 1954 and later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1977 to 2002.

François Lachaud (born 1965) works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, where he is attested as a professor in 2008 and with an affiliation attested in 2013.

Françoise Pommaret (born 1954) specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at Sorbonne University, INALCO, and the University of Paris. Her career includes posts at INALCO, the Royal University of Bhutan (~2008), and CNRS (2002, ~2004).

Françoise Robin (born 1968) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She studied at INALCO and under Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). Her career includes leadership roles at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).

Fred Pfeil (1949–2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned degrees from Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973), and taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (~1985–2005).

Freda Bedi (1911–1977) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College (~1929–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1953), and founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling.

Frederick James Furnivall (1825–1910) was a linguist educated at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910) and taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1870).

Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his academic career at the University of Minnesota from around 1971 to 2021, serving as a professor from around 1982 to 2021.
Frederick M. Smith is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He was a student of Ludo Rocher and held a position as a professor at the University of Iowa, attested between 2006 and 2008.

Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, he served at the India Office Library (1898–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He led the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) was an anthropologist who studied at the University of Chicago and University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

Friederike Assandri works in sinology and religious studies. She studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and pursued doctoral studies at Heidelberg University, where she later held a post attested in 2013.

Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral work at the University of Oxford. He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987) and Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed PhDs at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours, and was a professor at Indiana University (1964–1982) and Hamburg (1982–1993).

Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp, and held professorships at University College London (1828–1831) and the University of London (1834).

Friedrich August Wolf (1759–1824) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1777–1779) under Christian Gottlob Heyne and held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1783–1807).
